title: Closed [e] — é, -er, -ez, -ed, et, les/des/mes (set 1)
sounds: les / des / mes / tes / ses / ces
focus: All of these make the closed [e]: lips spread, tongue high, a pure « ay » with no glide at the end. It's spelled é; -er, -ez and -ed at the end of a word (parler, chez, pied); the word « et »; and the short words les, des, mes, tes, ses, ces. Exceptions: in a few short words the -er is [ɛʁ] with the r pronounced (mer, fer, hiver, cher, hier), and « est » has the open [ɛ]. Québécois keeps é and è clearly apart, even at the end of a word (« parlé » vs « parlait »).

sentences.fr: Le matin, j'aime boire un caf[é] au lait.
sentences.en: In the morning, I like to drink a café au lait.

sentences.fr: Je vais au caf[é] du quarti[er] avec m[es] amis.
sentences.en: I go to the neighbourhood café with my friends.

sentences.fr: Nous aimons parl[er] [et] mang[er] d[es] muffins.
sentences.en: We like to talk and eat muffins.

sentences.fr: La serveuse demande : « Vous d[é]sir[ez] autre chose ? »
sentences.en: The waitress asks: "Would you like anything else?"

sentences.fr: Il est d[é]jà dix heures : il faut travaill[er] !
sentences.en: It's already ten o'clock: time to work!
